# Jubilees Chapter 18 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** The Binding of Isaac; The Test; Mastema Loses; Annual Celebration

---

**18:1** In the seventh week, first year, first month of this jubilee — on the twelfth day — God called to Abraham: "Abraham, Abraham." He answered: "Here I am."

**18:2** God said: "Take your son — your only son, the one you love, Isaac — and go to the high country. Offer him as a burnt offering on one of the mountains I'll show you."

**18:3** Abraham got up before dawn, saddled his donkey, took two servants and his son Isaac, split the wood for the offering, and set out. They traveled for three days and reached the place.

**18:4** Abraham looked up and saw it from a distance.

**18:5** He told his servants: "Wait here with the donkey. The boy and I will go up there to worship and come back."

**18:6** Abraham put the wood on Isaac's back, took the fire and the knife, and the two of them walked up together.

**18:7** Isaac said: "Father?" "Yes, son?" "We have the fire and the wood — but where is the lamb for the offering?"

**18:8** Abraham said: "God will provide the lamb, son." And the two of them kept walking together.

**18:9** They arrived at the place God had designated. Abraham built the altar, arranged the wood, bound his son Isaac, and laid him on the altar on top of the wood.

**18:10** Abraham reached out his hand and picked up the knife to kill his son.

**18:11** I called out to him from heaven: "Abraham, Abraham!" He said: "Here I am."

**18:12** I said: "Don't touch the boy. Don't do anything to him. I know now that you truly fear God — you didn't hold back your son, your only son, from me."

**18:13** Abraham looked up and saw a ram behind him, its horns tangled in a thicket. He went and took the ram and offered it as a burnt offering in his son's place.

**18:14** Abraham named that place "The LORD will provide" — which is why people still say today: "On the mountain of the LORD it will be seen."

**18:15** Then the angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven a second time: "I swear by myself — this is the LORD's declaration — because you did this, because you did not hold back your son, your only son:"

**18:16** "I will bless you enormously. I will multiply your descendants until they are as countless as the stars in the sky and the grains of sand on the beach. Your descendants will conquer their enemies."

**18:17** "And through your descendants, every nation on earth will be blessed — because you listened and obeyed."

**18:18** Abraham went back to his servants, and they all returned together to Beersheba, where Abraham settled.

**18:19** Every year after that Abraham returned to that mountain, built an altar at the spot where he had first built one, and called out the name of the LORD: "The LORD, the everlasting God."

**18:20** He kept this as an annual celebration on that mountain — seven days of eating, drinking, and blessing the LORD God who had chosen him and brought him out of Ur of the Chaldees and sealed a covenant with him.

**18:21** When the prince Mastema saw all this play out, he was humiliated. And Abraham went on being perfect in everything he did before the LORD — his name honored before God every day of his life.

**18:22** Through every test the LORD put him through, he came out faithful. He loved God with his whole soul, clung to him, never hesitated, never grew weary — because his love for God was absolute.

---
*PNEUMA notes: The first-person shift (vv.11-12) — "I called," "I said" — identifies the narrator as the restraining angel. "I know now" (v.12) is rendered to preserve the dramatic tension of the divine acknowledgment. Mastema's humiliation (v.21) is the payoff of the whole Job-like setup.*
